transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ames (Redwood AE), Priya Kothari (Redwood SE), Mark Delgado (Crescent Bank Head of AI), Sarah Lee (Eng Manager), Tom Bannister (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Goal: scope a 6-week POC for Crescent Bank to evaluate Redwood inference for real-time customer support summarization and transactional routing. Confirm success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and commercial guardrails (pilot credits, terms, procurement path).
- Outcomes: agreed to run two benchmark runs (hosted + dedicated sim), pilot credit proposal (USD 50k credits + optional dedicated trial), and follow-ups to share security docs and SOW.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. I - uh - we'll give a quick intro. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side, and Priya our SE will drive the technical bits. Mark, do you want to kick off with context?
[00:18] Mark: Yeah, sure. Thanks Jordan. So Crescent is looking to POC a couple of things, mostly real-time summarization of customer chats and a light-weight routing model for transactional intents. Our main constraints are latency under 250ms p50 for short summaries, and predictable cost. We also have strict security needs — SOC2, SSO, KMS, etc.
[00:40] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick clarifying question — are you planning to use hosted Redwood API for the POC or test dedicated capacity / private?
[00:48] Sarah: Initially hosted to start fast, but we'd like to validate dedicated throughput for the high-volume peaks. We may want a Dedicated trial to test autoscaling and consistent p95.
[00:58] Tom: from security: we need details on encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also any possibility of private deployment if procurement requires it.
[01:10] Jordan: Yep, totally. We'll share the SOC2 report and a network diagram. We do offer Redwood Dedicated and Private. For the pilot commercial guardrails we typically propose credits to cover usage and a clearly defined scope — e.g., up to $50k in credits for token usage plus up to two dedicated trial days for throughput testing.
[01:29] Mark: That sounds reasonable. How do you measure success? We're looking for accuracy on summarization (ROUGE-ish baseline?) and latency/cost targets.
[01:38] Priya: Our recommended success criteria set usually has three pillars: latency targets (p50/p95), quality metrics on your eval prompts (we can run a golden-set of X=500 prompts), and operational metrics (error rate, retries, KV cache hit rates). For quality we can do both automated metrics and a small human eval.
[01:57] Sarah: For sizing — current volume is about 8k conversations per day, avg 120 tokens per summary, peak concurrency ~120 req/s during business hours.
[02:09] Priya: OK that's helpful. Quick back-of-envelope: hosted with our medium model (redwood-ml-medium-2025) with batching and prefix KV cache should meet p50 ~120-180ms for 120-token summaries, but p95 depends on burst controls and batching windows. For predictable p95 we usually recommend dedicated nodes with configured autoscaling and burst capacity.
[02:34] Mark: Can you run benchmarks that mirror these numbers? We'd like a hosted run first and then a dedicated sim with the same workload.
[02:41] Priya: Absolutely — we'll prepare a benchmark harness. We'll need the exact prompt set, token distributions, and concurrency profile. We'll also provide scripts to reproduce the run.
[02:52] Jordan: On the commercial side, our standard POC terms are: a time-boxed pilot (4-6 weeks), pilot credits that apply to usage, and an optional short-term dedicated trial for throughput testing. If Crescent wants a longer trial or reserved capacity, we move into a contracted Dedicated pilot with MSA/SOW.
[03:10] Tom: What's contained in the credits? Does it cover dedicated trial infra costs or just per-token usage on hosted? And what about data retention?
[03:19] Jordan: Credits typically cover hosted API usage (tokens, embeddings) and technical support hours. Dedicated trial infra for on-prem or reserved GPUs is usually a separate line item but we can include limited dedicated trial time in the pilot package (e.g., two days of dedicated cluster testing). Data retention and logs: hosted requests are retained for X days by default, we can provide options for shorter retention and for Private deployments you control logs. We'll share the data retention policy doc.
[03:45] Mark: Good. Procurement path — what's typical timeline to go from POC to contract? We have procurement windows and buying committees.
[03:53] Jordan: Typical flow: pilot -> procurement triggers (if pilot successful) -> commercial terms (committed capacity / annual) -> legal review. For mid-market banks like you the procurement cycle is 6-10 weeks after a successful pilot. We can pre-seed an SOW and attach standard terms to speed it up.
[04:12] Sarah: Any compliance packages or dedicated SOC/ISO evidence we can present internally?
[04:18] Jordan: Yes — SOC2 type II, ISO 27001 summary, encryption & key management whitepaper. We'll drop links: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf and https://redwood.example.com/security/network-diagram.pdf.
[04:30] Tom: We'll need SAML SSO and RBAC to be validated. Also audit log retention and access controls.
[04:37] Priya: We support SAML, SCIM user sync, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. For KMS we integrate with common providers and can do customer-managed keys for Private deployments. We'll include the integration notes in the security packet.
[04:53] Mark: Back to benchmarks — can you include model variants? We want to see cost/perf tradeoffs (medium vs small quantized).
[04:59] Priya: Yep — we'll run three variants in the harness: full fp16 medium, int8 quantized medium, and a smaller low-cost model. We'll report latency distributions, token cost, and quality delta on the eval set. That will help decide a quantization strategy.
[05:15] Jordan: For commercial guardrails, a typical pilot offer we discussed: 6-week pilot, USD 50k credits applied to usage, up to 24 hours of SE support included, and two days of dedicated cluster testing (if you want). If Crescent accepts, we provide an MSA + SOW to cover pilot scope and success criteria.
[05:36] Sarah: If we go to procurement after the pilot, what's the path to Dedicated reserved capacity and pricing?
[05:41] Jordan: We'll provide tiered pricing: pay-as-you-go for hosted, then reserved monthly for Dedicated with commit levels. The SOW can outline optional conversion credits if you convert pilot spend into committed capacity within 60 days.
[05:54] Mark: One of our concerns is noisy neighbor and multi-tenant variability on hosted — will dedicated remove that?
[06:01] Priya: Yes, Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and more predictable tail latency. We also have routing policies to keep critical traffic on dedicated nodes and failover to hosted variants if capacity is constrained.
[06:13] Tom: A question on data residency — we operate in EU and US and need certain data to stay in-region. Can Redwood pin region for hosted?
[06:21] Jordan: Yes, region routing is configurable; we can ensure EU requests stay in EU. For regulated flows we often recommend Private or Dedicated in the same region with customer-managed networking.
[06:33] Mark: Costs — can you provide an estimate for our 8k conv/day workload?
[06:38] Priya: We'll produce a workbook. Rough ballpark: if average summary is 120 tokens and you do 8k/day that's ~960k tokens/day. Multiply by our hosted token rate and apply batching efficiencies; with credits we'll show net cost. We'll include three scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[06:56] Sarah: About success criteria — we want explicit pass/fail: e.g., average summarization quality >= baseline by X% and p95 latency < 350ms under peak concurrency.
[07:07] Priya: Agree. We'll propose concrete numeric thresholds and a test harness. Human eval will be a small sample (50-100 examples) and automated metrics on full 500-example golden set.
[07:18] Jordan: On SLAs: pilot doesn't include formal uptime SLA, but Dedicated can carry SLA in contract. We'll also include runbooks and tracing hooks in the Console for you to observe per-route latency and cost.
[07:32] Mark: Any caveats on the scoring metrics? We use proprietary scoring — can you plug that into the harness?
[07:38] Priya: Yes — you can provide a scoring script or we can run our harness against your scoring function. We'll need it 48 hours before the first benchmark.
[07:49] Tom: Are there any security red flags we should know about — e.g. third-party model dependencies?
[07:54] Jordan: Most models we host are open-source variants; we validate licenses. For sensitive data we recommend Private or Dedicated with KM-backed encryption. We'll include a model licensing summary.
[08:07] Mark: Procurement note — our CFO will ask about termination rights, data deletion, and transfer of logs.
[08:14] Jordan: All can be addressed in the SOW/MSA; we'll highlight data deletion timelines and escrow of logs if required.
[08:22] Sarah: For the pilot timeline can we start next week? We have a sprint window opening Monday.
[08:28] Jordan: We can kick off as early as next Wednesday pending paperwork. Typical timeline: 1) sign pilot SOW / NDAs, 2) share prompts & workloads, 3) run hosted benchmark (week 1), 4) dedicated trial (week 2-3), 5) evaluation and human review (week 4-5), 6) wrap and decision. That's about 4-6 weeks.
[08:49] Mark: Fine. From procurement side, we'll need an indicative pilot cost summary and an outline of steps to expedite contracting.
[08:56] Jordan: We'll include an accelerated procurement checklist and suggested timeline.
[09:02] Priya: Technical detail — for bench harness we will instrument token-level latency, KV cache hit rates, and batching windows. We'll also collect GPU metrics for the dedicated sim.
[09:14] Mark: Good. Can you list what logs we will get in the Console? We need per-token cost, per-request latency, and trace IDs for our app telemetry.
[09:22] Jordan: Yes — per-route dashboards, trace sampling, and cost breakdown. We'll share a screenshot of the Console and a sample CSV export.
[09:31] Sarah: Any references or previous case studies for banks or regulated customers?
[09:36] Jordan: We'll share a short case study and a reference list — e.g., Nova Health and Horizon Health POCs (see links we send).
[09:46] Tom: Ok security follow-ups to include: SOC2 report, KMS integration doc, SAML config guide, and network diagram.
[09:53] Jordan: We'll drop those in the shared folder.
[09:58] Mark: Last question on conversion credits — if we convert to a committed Dedicated contract, how much of pilot spend is applied?
[10:06] Jordan: Standard is up to 50% conversion credit of pilot consumption if you convert within 60 days, negotiated in the SOW. We'll note that in the pilot terms doc.
[10:17] Sarah: That will help procurement.
[10:20] Jordan: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[10:24] Priya: I'll list technical items: need workload samples, scoring script, and access for benchmark.
[10:29] Jordan: Commercial items: pilot pricing sheet, credits table, SOW draft, and security packet. I'll own the pricing and SOW.
[10:35] Mark: We'll get you the workloads and scoring by Friday.
[10:38] Tom: I'll confirm KMS/VPC notes within the week.
[10:42] Jordan: Perfect. We'll aim to have the pricing & SOW to you by 2025-11-20 and the benchmark scripts by 2025-11-19.
[10:50] Sarah: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:53] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark run and the SOW.
[11:00] [meeting ends]
